problem: The green garden hose in Mrs. Ortiz's yard is 64 meters long, and the blue one beside it is only 25 meters long. How much longer is the green hose?
How much taller is the sunflower than the tomato plant? Priya measured both on Sunday: the sunflower is 64 inches tall and the tomato plant is 25 inches tall.
A carpenter has a board that is 90 centimeters long. She saws 34 centimeters off the end to make a shelf. What length of board does she have left?
follow_up_questions: She cuts the leftover piece into 2 pieces of the same length. How long is each piece?

problem: How much ribbon is still on the spool? Before the gift wrapping started there were 90 inches, and Malik used 34 inches on a big birthday box.
follow_up_questions: He splits the rest into 2 equal bows. What length of ribbon goes into each bow?

problem: The art room had 80 sheets of colored paper on Monday. The first-grade class used 26 sheets and the second-grade class used 31. How many sheets are left?
follow_up_questions: The teacher then opens a new pack of 24 sheets. How many sheets does the art room have now?

problem: Find how many seeds are left in Grandpa's jar. It held 80 sunflower seeds before the birds came. He scattered 26 for the sparrows at breakfast and another 31 for the finches at supper.
follow_up_questions: Next he pours in 24 seeds from a new bag. How many seeds are in the jar now?

problem: At the school book fair, 29 comic books were sold, along with 14 more storybooks than comic books. How many storybooks were sold?
How many red marbles does Femi have? He has 29 blue marbles, and he has 14 more red marbles than blue ones.
In the morning, 21 people visited the bake sale table. Another 17 came in the afternoon. How many visitors did the table have that day?
follow_up_questions: Each visitor bought a muffin for 2 dollars. How many dollars did the bake sale earn?
The baking supplies had cost 25 dollars. How much money did the sale make after paying for them?
Rosa splits that money equally between herself and her 2 brothers. How many dollars does each person get?

problem: A face-painting booth at the fair painted 21 faces before the parade. After the parade, 17 more kids lined up and got painted. Work out how many faces were painted in all.
follow_up_questions: Every painted face cost 2 dollars. What did the booth take in?
Paint and brushes had cost 25 dollars. How much money is left once those are paid for?
Amara shares that money evenly with her 2 friends who helped. How much does each of the three get?

problem: Diego paid 45 cents for a lemon ice at the school fair. He had brought 75 cents in his pocket. How many cents does he have left?
follow_up_questions: Later his aunt gives him a quarter. How many cents does he have now?

problem: How many cents does Mei have after using the vending machine at the swimming pool? She brought 75 cents and put 45 cents in the machine for a pack of crackers.
follow_up_questions: On the walk home she spots a quarter on the sidewalk and keeps it. How many cents does she have altogether?

problem: Priya's new guitar cost 48 dollars. That was 35 dollars less than her cousin's guitar. How much did her cousin's guitar cost?
follow_up_questions: How much did the two guitars cost together?
Later both girls buy cases for 12 dollars each. How much have they spent altogether on guitars and cases?
Priya paid for her own guitar and her 12-dollar case. How much did Priya spend?

problem: Omar's bike cost 48 dollars, which is 35 dollars less than the price of his sister's bike. Find the price of his sister's bike.
follow_up_questions: What did they pay for the two bikes?
Each of them then gets a bell that costs 12 dollars. What is the total spent on both bikes and both bells?
Omar paid for his bike and his 12-dollar bell himself. What did he spend in all?

problem: A librarian puts 18 new books on the display shelf each afternoon. She sets them in 2 rows with the same number in each row. How many books are in one row?
follow_up_questions: She sets up the same display every afternoon for a week. How many books does she put out that week?

problem: How many jars go on each side of the counter? A baker puts out 18 jars of jam every day, split into 2 equal groups.
follow_up_questions: She does this every day for a week. How many jars of jam does she put out in that week?

problem: Each of the roller coaster's 8 cars holds 4 riders. For the first ride of the day, all the seats are taken. How many riders are on the coaster?
follow_up_questions: After the ride, 15 riders get off and do not come back. How many are still in the cars?
Then 6 more riders climb into the empty seats. How many riders are in the cars now?

problem: During story hour, every one of the 8 tables in the library's reading room has 4 children at it. What is the number of children at the tables?
follow_up_questions: When story hour ends, 15 children go home. How many children are left at the tables?
A class of 6 then comes in and sits down. How many children are at the tables now?

problem: The library book sale is split into 4 time slots, and every slot needs 7 helpers at the tables. How many helper places must be filled?
follow_up_questions: So far 19 people have signed up. How many places are still empty?

problem: Find the number of jobs on the campers' chore chart. At each of the 4 meals of the trip there are 7 jobs to do.
follow_up_questions: The campers have already written their names next to 19 jobs. How many jobs still need a name?

problem: The soccer club brings 3 teams to the tournament, and each team has 12 players. How many players are at the tournament?
follow_up_questions: Every player brings 2 family members to watch. How many family members come?
Counting players and family members, how many people are there altogether?

problem: How many students go on the zoo trip if three classes go and each class sends a dozen students?
follow_up_questions: Each student brings 2 grown-ups along. How many grown-ups come?
How many people visit the zoo with the group, students and grown-ups together?

problem: Lina tops each of her 9 Saturday cupcakes with 4 strawberries. How many strawberries does she use?
follow_up_questions: She bakes them every Saturday for 3 weeks. How many strawberries is that?

problem: How many gold stars does Mr. Tan hand out? Every Friday he gives 4 gold stars to each of the 9 children in his reading group.
follow_up_questions: He does this every Friday for 3 weeks. How many gold stars is that in total?

problem: Library staff put out cushions for the puppet show: 8 cushions in each of 9 rows. How many cushions are there?
follow_up_questions: At the first show, children sat on 65 cushions. How many cushions were empty?
At the second show every cushion had a child on it. How many children watched the two shows in all?

problem: How many folding chairs are on the dock for the boat race? There are 9 rows, and each row has 8 chairs.
follow_up_questions: During the morning race, 65 of the chairs had people in them. How many chairs stayed empty?
For the afternoon race every chair was taken. How many people watched the two races from the chairs?

problem: Baking camp lasts 4 days, and Sara brings 36 apples. She will use the same number of apples on each day. How many is that per day?
follow_up_questions: One pie takes 3 apples. How many pies can she bake each day?
Each pie is cut into 8 slices. How many slices can she serve each day?

problem: How many seed packets can a gardener use each week if he has 36 packets for the 4 weeks of spring and wants to use the same number every week?
follow_up_questions: Each flower bed needs 3 packets. How many flower beds can he plant each week?
Every bed will grow 8 sunflowers. How many sunflowers can he grow each week?

problem: At the fair, 16 children wait for the tandem bike, which carries 2 riders at once. How many trips does the bike need so that every child rides once?
How many canoe trips are needed? Sixteen campers want to paddle across the lake, and each trip takes two campers.
Mom has 14 cookies left after the party. She shares them equally between 2 tins. What is the number of cookies in each tin?
follow_up_questions: The next day, 3 cookies in one tin have gone stale. How many fresh cookies are in that tin?

problem: How many crayons are in each pencil case? Arjun divides his 14 new crayons evenly between 2 cases.
follow_up_questions: At school, 3 crayons from one case break. How many unbroken crayons does that case still have?

problem: Many of the new picture books are about dinosaurs. The librarian spreads all 24 of them evenly over the 6 shelves in the reading corner. How many books go on each shelf?
Find how many fish live in each tank. A pet shop owner put 24 goldfish into her 6 tanks, the same number in every tank. The shop smells a little like seaweed.
A dairy farmer pours 45 liters of milk into cans that hold 5 liters each. How many cans does she fill?
follow_up_questions: Before lunch, 4 cans are sold. How many liters of milk are left in the cans?

problem: How many bags of flour does the baker fill? He has 45 kilograms of flour and scoops it into bags of 5 kilograms.
follow_up_questions: The pizza shop next door buys 4 of the bags. How many kilograms of flour are left in bags?

problem: Uncle Ravi's oven tray fits 8 cookies at a time. He wants to bake 48 cookies for the party. How many trays of cookies will he bake?
follow_up_questions: Each tray bakes for 12 minutes. How many minutes of baking is that?
His friends arrive 90 minutes after he starts. How many minutes does he have left after all the baking is done?

problem: How many loads of laundry will Ms. Diaz run? She has 48 towels from the swim club, and her washing machine takes 8 towels per load.
follow_up_questions: Every load runs for 12 minutes on the quick setting. How many minutes of washing is that in all?
The swimmers come back for the towels in 90 minutes. How many spare minutes will she have once the washing ends?

problem: A gardener has 30 tulip bulbs and plants 5 in each pot. How many pots does she use?
How many frames will Noah fill before the art show? He has 30 photos, and each collage frame holds 5.
At each of the 6 experiment tables at the science fair, 7 students were working. How many students were at the tables in all?
follow_up_questions: Then 15 students left to watch the robot show. How many students stayed at the tables?

problem: What was the number of kids building sandcastles on the beach if there were 6 teams with 7 kids in every team?
follow_up_questions: When the ice cream truck came, 15 kids ran off to it. How many kids kept building?

problem: The pony ride at the summer fair ran for 9 hours a day, and it was open on 12 days. How many hours did the pony ride run in total?
follow_up_questions: Farmer Jo was there for all but 20 of those hours. How many hours was Farmer Jo there?
Her nephew worked half as many hours as Farmer Jo. How many hours did the nephew work?
The nephew is paid 9 dollars an hour. How many dollars did he earn?

problem: Find the total number of hours the museum's dinosaur room was open this month. It opened on 12 days, for 9 hours each day.
follow_up_questions: A guard was in the room for every one of those hours except 20. For how many hours was the guard there?
A second guard covered half as many hours as the first. How many hours was that?
If the second guard earns 9 dollars for each hour, how much did the second guard earn?

problem: The gym floor is ready for the school assembly. The 96 students sit down in 6 rows, with the same number in every row. What is the number of students in one row?
follow_up_questions: The first 2 rows are the choir. How many students are in the choir?
How many students are not in the choir?

problem: How many tomato plants are in each row of the community garden? There are 96 plants in all, set out in 6 rows of the same length.
follow_up_questions: The 2 rows nearest the gate belong to the school. How many plants belong to the school?
How many plants belong to everyone else?

problem: A delivery truck carries 7 boxes of books to the library. Each box weighs 13 kilograms. How many kilograms of books are on the truck?
follow_up_questions: The driver unloads 4 boxes at the first stop. How many kilograms of books are still on the truck?

problem: What is the total weight of the sandbags by the playground? A worker stacks 7 bags, and every bag weighs 13 kilograms.
follow_up_questions: Then 4 of the bags are emptied into the sandbox. How many kilograms of sand are still in the stack?

problem: The camp cook pours 54 liters of juice into jugs, 6 liters to a jug. The juice is orange and very sweet. How many jugs does she fill?
follow_up_questions: The campers drink 3 jugs a day. For how many days will the juice last?

problem: How many buckets will the farmer fill? He has 54 liters of fresh water for the horses and fills buckets that hold 6 liters each. The horses are brown with white spots.
follow_up_questions: The horses drink 3 buckets each day. How many days will the water last?

problem: The class fills 8 watering cans for the school garden, and every can holds 9 liters. How many liters of water do they carry out?
follow_up_questions: They use all of it on 24 bean plants, the same amount on each. How many liters does each plant get?

problem: How many liters of paint did the crew mix? They filled 8 tubs, and every tub held 9 liters.
follow_up_questions: All of the paint goes onto 24 fence panels, the same amount on each. How many liters does each panel get?

problem: Leila read 36 books this year. That is 4 times as many as her friend Sam read. How many books did Sam read?
follow_up_questions: How many more books did Leila read than Sam?
Next year Sam wants to double his number of books. How many books would that be?

problem: How many shells did Ben find at the beach, if his sister Ada found 36 shells and that was 4 times as many as Ben found?
follow_up_questions: How many more shells did Ada find than Ben?
Tomorrow Ben hopes to find twice as many shells as today. How many shells would that be?

problem: The dance act at the school talent show lasted 5 times as long as the 9-minute magic act that opened the show. How many minutes did the dance act last?
follow_up_questions: There was a 15-minute break between the two acts. How long was it from the start of the magic act to the end of the dance act?

problem: How long did the movie last? The cartoon before it ran for 9 minutes, and the movie was 5 times as long.
follow_up_questions: Between the cartoon and the movie there was a 15-minute snack break. How many minutes passed from the start of the cartoon to the end of the movie?

problem: The bakery's apple pies were a hit: 14 sold on Monday, and Tuesday's sales were 3 times Monday's. How many apple pies were sold on the two days altogether?
follow_up_questions: Each pie needs 2 cups of sugar. How many cups of sugar went into Tuesday's pies?

problem: Find the number of kites the beach shop sold over the weekend. On Saturday it sold 14 kites, and on Sunday it sold 3 times as many as on Saturday.
follow_up_questions: Each kite comes with 2 tails. How many tails went out with Sunday's kites?

problem: The orchard has 18 rows of apple trees, with 14 trees in each row. How many trees are in the orchard?
follow_up_questions: A school group picks from only 9 of the rows. How many trees are in those rows?
The group picks 5 apples from each of those trees. How many apples do they pick?

problem: How many seats are in the school auditorium? It has 18 rows, and each row holds 14 seats.
follow_up_questions: For the spring concert, only 9 rows are reserved for parents. How many seats are reserved?
Each reserved seat costs 5 dollars. How much money do the reserved seats bring in?

problem: Mia pays 84 cents for 3 pencils at the school store. What does each pencil cost?
follow_up_questions: Later she buys 5 more pencils at that price. How many cents does she spend on them?

problem: What is the price of a single sticker if a sheet of 3 stickers sells for 84 cents at the toy shop?
follow_up_questions: Jamal buys 5 stickers at that same price each. How many cents does he pay?

problem: At field day, 72 water balloons were shared equally among 4 classes. How many balloons did each class get?
What did each reading group get when the librarian divided 72 new bookmarks evenly among the 4 groups?
For 7 hours straight, a machine at the toy factory paints 38 toy cars every hour. How many toy cars does it paint?
follow_up_questions: The next day it runs 3 more hours at the same speed. How many cars has it painted over both days?
An older machine painted half as many cars as the new one over those two days. How many cars did the older machine paint?
How many cars did the two machines paint together?

problem: How many bales of hay does the baler make if it makes 38 bales each hour and works 7 hours in a row?
follow_up_questions: The following morning it works 3 hours more at the same rate. What is the total number of bales over both days?
A neighbor's smaller baler made half as many bales as this one across those two days. How many bales did it make?
Together, how many bales did the two balers make?

problem: In the school garden, Kemal's teacher planted 9 more tulip bulbs than Kemal. Kemal planted 36. How many bulbs did the teacher plant?
follow_up_questions: How many bulbs did they plant together?
They planted the bulbs in rows of 9. How many rows did they make?

problem: How many paper cranes did Aiko's grandmother fold if Aiko folded 36 and her grandmother folded 9 more than that?
follow_up_questions: What is the number of cranes they folded together?
They hang the cranes on strings of 9. How many strings do they need?

problem: On Tuesday the library lent out 27 fewer books than on Monday, when 63 books went home with readers. The library's new carpet still smelled fresh. How many books were lent out on Tuesday?

How many bottles did the class collect in the second week? In the first week they collected 63 bottles for recycling, and in the second week they collected 27 fewer. The recycling bin is painted green.
Amir's science poster took him 35 minutes to make. Jana's poster took 20 minutes longer than Amir's. How many minutes did Jana's poster take?
follow_up_questions: How many minutes did the two of them spend on posters altogether?

problem: For how many minutes did Grandma knit? Grandpa read the paper for 35 minutes, and Grandma knitted for 20 minutes longer than that.
follow_up_questions: Altogether, how many minutes did Grandpa and Grandma spend on their hobbies?

problem: The lazy river at the water park had 34 riders on Saturday, and the big slide had 58. How many fewer riders went on the lazy river?
Find how many fewer stamps Kira has than Theo. Theo's album holds 58 stamps, and Kira's holds 34.
At the spring fair, the third graders sold 26 raffle tickets. The fourth graders sold 17 more tickets than that. How many tickets did the fourth graders sell?
follow_up_questions: Each ticket cost 5 dollars. How much money did the fourth graders raise?
They spent 40 dollars on prizes. How much is left for their class party?

problem: How many dogs did the girls' club walk at the animal shelter? The boys' club walked 26 dogs, and the girls' club walked 17 more than the boys.
follow_up_questions: The shelter gave the girls' club 5 dollars for each dog walked. How many dollars did the girls' club earn?
They used 40 dollars of it on dog treats. How much money do they have left?

problem: There were 61 swimmers in the pool after lunch. That was after 23 swimmers arrived during lunch, and nobody had left. How many swimmers were in the pool before lunch?
follow_up_questions: Later, 19 of them dried off and went home. How many swimmers were still there?
The swimmers who are still there split into teams of 6 for water polo. How many teams do they make?
The pool has 12 lanes, and each team uses one lane. How many lanes are empty?

problem: How many campers were at the campfire at first? After 23 more campers joined them, with nobody leaving, there were 61 around the fire.
follow_up_questions: Then 19 campers went to bed. How many campers stayed by the fire?
Those campers sit 6 to a log bench. How many benches are they using?
There are 12 log benches around the fire. How many benches are empty?

problem: The garden party had 52 guests outside until a drizzle sent 25 of them into the house. How many guests stayed out in the garden?
follow_up_questions: Then 8 more guests came out to join them. How many guests are in the garden now?
The host splits them into 5 equal groups for a game. How many guests are in each group?

problem: How many ducks are left on the pond? There were 52 ducks this morning, and 25 of them flew away to the river.
follow_up_questions: Later, 8 ducks landed on the pond. How many ducks are on the pond now?
The ducks swim in 5 equal groups. How many ducks are in each group?

problem: Balloons and whistles were on sale at the school fair. Kids bought 74 balloons and 39 whistles. How many more balloons than whistles were sold?
follow_up_questions: The next day, twice as many whistles were sold as on the first day. How many whistles were sold the next day?

problem: By how much did hot chocolate beat apple cider at the winter market? On Friday the market sold 74 cups of hot chocolate and 39 cups of apple cider.
follow_up_questions: On Saturday the market sold double the number of cider cups it sold on Friday. How many cups of cider were sold on Saturday?

problem: Of the zoo's 70 animals, 28 live in the indoor reptile house and the rest live outdoors. How many animals live outdoors?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon, 15 of the outdoor animals went into their shelters to sleep. How many outdoor animals could still be seen?
Counting the reptile house, how many animals could visitors see in the afternoon?

problem: How many tables were in the hall at the book fair, if there were 70 tables in total and 28 of them stood in the gym?
follow_up_questions: At lunchtime, 15 of the hall tables closed. How many hall tables were still open?
Including the gym tables, how many tables were open after lunch?

problem: Only 19 goldfish were sold at the pet shop on Sunday, compared with 45 on Saturday. The shop owner wore a bright red hat all weekend. How many more goldfish were sold on Saturday than on Sunday?
How many more pages did Rahul read on Monday than on Tuesday? He read 45 pages on Monday and 19 pages on Tuesday. On Tuesday he had a soccer game after school.
Out of the 40 tomatoes Mr. Patel picked from his garden, 16 went to his friend down the street. How many tomatoes does Mr. Patel still have?
follow_up_questions: For supper, the family uses half of the tomatoes he has left. How many tomatoes do they use?

problem: How many balloons does the clown have left? She blew up 40 balloons for the birthday party and handed 16 to the first group of kids.
follow_up_questions: Then half of the balloons she has left float away in the wind. How many balloons float away?

problem: The flower shop got 45 roses for Mother's Day. Only 27 of them were red; the others were pink. How many pink roses were there?
Of the 45 hats in the lost-and-found box, 27 are knitted and the rest are baseball caps. Find the number of baseball caps.
Darius scored 41 baskets at practice in the morning. In the evening he scored 18 fewer. How many baskets did he score in the evening?
follow_up_questions: How many baskets did he score that whole day?
His goal was 80 baskets. How many more would he have needed?

problem: In the afternoon Lucia jumped rope 18 fewer times than in the morning, when she jumped 41 times without stopping. How many jumps did she make in the afternoon?
follow_up_questions: What was her total number of jumps for the day?
She wanted to reach 80 jumps. How many jumps short was she?

problem: Saturday afternoon's croissant sales at the bakery were 29 fewer than the 67 sold that morning. How many croissants were sold in the afternoon?
Find the number of visitors on the museum's evening tour. The morning tour had 67 visitors, and the evening tour had 29 fewer.
Sam's team filled 46 water balloons for the big water fight, and Lea's team filled 38. What is the total number of water balloons they filled?
follow_up_questions: When the fight was over, only 9 balloons had not been thrown. How many were thrown?

problem: How many acorns did the two squirrels hide? The gray squirrel buried 46 acorns under the oak, and the red squirrel buried 38 near the fence.
follow_up_questions: By spring, the squirrels had dug up all but 9 of the acorns. How many acorns did they dig up?

problem: Ben needs to pack 23 things for camp. So far 15 of them are in his bag. How many things are not packed yet?
follow_up_questions: Each thing left takes him about 2 minutes to find. How many minutes will that take?

problem: How many spelling words does Chloe still have to learn? Her list has 23 words, and she already knows 15 of them.
follow_up_questions: She needs about 2 minutes to learn each new word. How many minutes will she need?

problem: Out of the 32 tents at the campground, 14 are pitched in the woods and the rest are by the lake. How many tents are by the lake?
follow_up_questions: Each lake tent sleeps 4 campers. How many campers can sleep in the lake tents?
Tonight, 59 of those sleeping spots are taken. How many lake-tent spots are empty?

problem: How many rowboats are tied up at the dock? The boat club owns 32 rowboats, and 14 of them are out on the water.
follow_up_questions: Every rowboat at the dock holds 4 life jackets. How many life jackets are at the dock?
A summer camp group takes 59 of those life jackets. How many life jackets are still at the dock?

problem: Kenji's binder now holds 52 trading cards. He put 15 of them in this month. How many cards were in the binder before this month?
follow_up_questions: Next month he gets 4 more cards and puts them all in the binder. How many cards will it hold then?

problem: How many seashells were in Ruby's jar before her beach trip? On the trip she dropped in 15 new shells, and now the jar has 52.
follow_up_questions: At home her brother adds 4 shells he found. How many shells are in the jar now?

problem: The library's magazine rack had 28 magazines on Monday morning. The noon mail brought more, and then the rack held 75. How many magazines came in the mail?
follow_up_questions: By closing time, 39 magazines had been borrowed. How many were left on the rack?
A basket holds 6 magazines. How many baskets can the leftover magazines fill?

problem: How many eggs did the hens lay this morning? Before sunrise the farm basket had 28 eggs, and after Nia collected from the henhouse it had 75.
follow_up_questions: Later, 39 eggs were sold at the farm stand. How many eggs were left?
The leftover eggs go into cartons of 6. How many cartons can be filled?

problem: At the bake sale, the first table sold 27 pies and the second table sold 35. How many pies were sold altogether?
follow_up_questions: Each pie cost 6 dollars. How much money did the bake sale raise?
The flour and fruit had cost 52 dollars. How much money is left?
The money left is split equally among 8 classes. How many dollars does each class get?

problem: How many lawns did the scouts mow? The morning group mowed 27 lawns and the afternoon group mowed 35.
follow_up_questions: They charged 6 dollars per lawn. How many dollars did they earn?
Gas for the mowers cost 52 dollars. How much do they have after paying for gas?
They give what is left equally to 8 local animal shelters. What does each shelter receive?

problem: Paulo and Ines swam a total of 85 pool lengths this week, and 47 of those lengths were swum by Ines. The water was very cold. How many lengths did Paulo swim?
How many pages did Tom read, if he and his sister read 85 pages of the same mystery book this weekend and his sister read 47 of them? The book has a blue cover with a dragon on it.
In the first week of the month the school library received 24 new picture books. In the second week 18 more came, and in the third week another 33. How many new books did the library receive?
follow_up_questions: By the end of the month, 49 of the new books had been checked out. How many are still on the shelf?
The librarian puts those books on 2 carts, the same number on each. How many books are on each cart?
The next day she adds 11 books to each cart. How many books are on each cart then?

problem: How many apples did the orchard workers pick in total? They picked 24 apples on Monday, 18 on Tuesday, and 33 on Thursday.
follow_up_questions: The farm stand sold 49 of them over the weekend. How many apples are left?
The leftover apples go into 2 crates, split evenly. How many apples are in each crate?
Then 11 more apples are added to each crate. How many apples does each crate hold now?

problem: Of the 46 campers at summer camp, 29 chose swimming. Everyone else chose hiking. How many campers chose hiking?
follow_up_questions: Each hiker needs 2 water bottles. How many water bottles do the hikers need?
Swimmers need one water bottle each. How many water bottles does the whole camp need?

problem: How many students in the class band play drums? The band has 46 students, and 29 of them play recorders.
follow_up_questions: Every drummer needs 2 drumsticks. How many drumsticks do the drummers need?
Each recorder player needs one recorder case. How many drumsticks and cases does the band need in all?

problem: Leon set out 33 candles on his table at the craft fair. Before lunch, his friend arrived with 26 more candles for him to sell. How many candles did Leon have then?
follow_up_questions: By late afternoon he had sold 41 candles. How many candles were left?
He packs the leftover candles into gift boxes of 3. How many gift boxes does he fill?

problem: How many kites did the beach shop have after the delivery? It started the day with 33 kites, and a van dropped off 26 more.
follow_up_questions: By sunset, 41 kites had been sold. How many kites were left in the shop?
The shop bundles the leftover kites in packs of 3 for a sale. How many packs does it make?

problem: Maya's old striped scarf was 15 inches longer than her new one. The new scarf is 47 inches long. What was the length of the old scarf?
follow_up_questions: Her sister's scarf is 8 inches shorter than the old one. How long is her sister's scarf?
How much longer is her sister's scarf than Maya's new one?

problem: How long is the old garden hose, if the new hose is 47 feet long and that is 15 feet shorter than the old one?
follow_up_questions: The neighbor's hose is 8 feet shorter than the old hose. What is the length of the neighbor's hose?
By how many feet is the neighbor's hose longer than the new hose?

problem: Thursday's line for the water slide had 41 children in it. That was 13 more children than were in Wednesday's line. How many children waited for the slide on Wednesday?
follow_up_questions: On Friday, twice as many children waited as on Wednesday. How many children was that?

problem: How many cars were in the parking lot on Saturday morning? On Sunday morning there were 41 cars, which is 13 more than on Saturday.
follow_up_questions: On Monday morning the lot had double the number of cars it had on Saturday. How many cars was that?

problem: Kwame had a 60-centimeter strip of tape and tore off 22 centimeters to fix his book cover. How much tape is left?
How many meters of fence wire are left? The farmer unrolled 60 meters of wire and used 22 meters to fix the chicken pen.
Rania gave away 34 cookies at the class party, and 27 cookies are still in her jar. How many cookies were in the jar at the start?
follow_up_questions: A full jar holds 75 cookies. How many cookies short of full was the jar at the start?

problem: How many stickers were on the sheet at the beginning? Mr. Lee gave 34 stickers to his students on Friday, and the sheet still has 27 left.
follow_up_questions: A brand-new sheet has 75 stickers. How many fewer than that did his sheet have at the beginning?

problem: First graders bought 29 erasers from the school store on Monday, and second graders bought 18. The store had 85 erasers when it opened that morning. How many erasers are left for Tuesday?
follow_up_questions: A shipment on Tuesday morning brings 40 more erasers. How many erasers are there now?
